concerns.text: Task T001 is marked `[P]` (parallel‑safe) but creates the project root directory and several sub‑directories. Concurrent execution with other tasks that also write to the repository root (e.g., T002, T003, T004) would cause race conditions on the filesystem. This violates the parallel‑safety guarantee.

Task T002 adds a `.gitignore` at the project root and is also marked `[P]`. It shares the same file location as T001 and T003, so running it in parallel can lead to nondeterministic `.gitignore` content.
Task T003 writes `requirements.txt`. Marked `[P]`, yet it writes to a file that may be concurrently modified by other `[P]` tasks (e.g., T001, T002). This is not parallel‑safe.
Task T004 creates `quickstart.md`. As a `[P]` task it could race with T001‑T003 which also modify the repository root. The file creation is not independent of those writes.

Task T005 writes `code/config.py` and is marked `[P]`. Subsequent tasks (e.g., T009‑T012) read this config; running T005 in parallel with any consumer could lead to consumers reading a partially written config.

Task T006 updates the global state YAML file. It is marked `[P]` but later tasks (T014, T027) also invoke `code/update_state.py`, writing to the same state file. Parallel execution would cause nondeterministic hash maps.

Task T014 calls `code/update_state.py` after coefficient files are written. Since T006 also updates the state earlier, the two updates must be serialized; otherwise the later update may overwrite hashes from the earlier run.
Task T027 runs `code/update_state.py` after LOO artefacts are written. Like T014, it must not run concurrently with any other state‑updating task.
